summary: Tazarotene is a topical retinoid (a prodrug of tazarotenic acid) indicated for the topical treatment of plaque psoriasis and acne vulgaris. Applied as a thin layer once daily in the evening, it binds retinoic acid receptors to normalize keratinocyte differentiation. It is a teratogen and is contraindicated in pregnancy; common effects are local irritation, and it causes photosensitivity so sun protection is required.
indications: Topical treatment of plaque psoriasis (cream/gel 0.05% and 0.1%)

dosage.d: Apply a thin film (approximately 2 mg/cm2) once daily in the evening to cover only the psoriatic lesions
dosage.n: Start with 0.05%, increase to 0.1% if tolerated and indicated; apply to dry skin

dosage.d: Apply a thin layer of 0.1% once daily in the evening to the affected area
dosage.n: Cleanse and dry skin; apply only to affected areas

admin: For topical (cutaneous) use only - not for ophthalmic, oral, or intravaginal use
Apply a thin layer once daily in the evening to affected skin only
Cleanse and dry the skin before application; apply emollients at least an hour before if used
Wash hands thoroughly after application; if contact with eyes/mucous membranes occurs, rinse with water
Avoid application to eczematous skin (may cause severe irritation); use daily sunscreen and protective clothing
moa: Tazarotene is a retinoid prodrug that is converted to its active form, tazarotenic acid, by deesterification. Tazarotenic acid binds to all three members of the retinoic acid receptor (RAR) family - RAR alpha, beta, and gamma - with relative selectivity for RAR beta and gamma, and may modify gene expression involved in keratinocyte differentiation, proliferation, and inflammation. The precise clinical significance of these findings is unknown.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to any component of the product
relative: Concomitant use of other photosensitizing drugs
monitor: Negative pregnancy test within 2 weeks before starting in females of childbearing potential
Local skin reactions (pruritus, burning, redness, peeling)

preg: Tazarotene is contraindicated in pregnancy. Based on animal reproduction studies, retinoid pharmacology, and the potential for systemic absorption, it may cause fetal harm. Females of childbearing potential should have a negative pregnancy test within 2 weeks before initiating treatment and use an effective method of contraception during treatment; it should be discontinued as soon as pregnancy is recognized.
lact: It is not known whether tazarotene is present in human milk, but after topical application plasma levels of tazarotenic acid are low. Use with caution; to avoid infant exposure, do not apply directly to the breast/chest, and the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother's clinical need.
renal: No specific renal dose adjustment is described; systemic absorption after topical use is low.
hepatic: No specific hepatic dose adjustment is described; systemic absorption after topical use is low.

moderate: Photosensitizing drugs (e.g. thiazides, tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones, sulfonamides, phenothiazines) - additive photosensitivity
minor: Topical products with strong drying effects, alcohol, or abrasives - additive irritation
interactions.alcohol: No specific systemic interaction; avoid alcohol-containing topical products on treated skin (irritation)
interactions.diagnostics: No specific diagnostic test interference described

Contact irritation on application to unaffected or eczematous skin

counsel: Apply a thin layer once at night to affected skin only; wash your hands afterwards
Do not use if you are pregnant or planning pregnancy - use reliable contraception and tell your clinician if pregnancy occurs
Use sunscreen daily and avoid sunlamps and weather extremes; your skin is more prone to sunburn
Mild redness, burning, dryness, or peeling is common early; stop and contact your clinician if it becomes severe
Do not apply to broken, eczematous, or sunburned skin and keep away from eyes, mouth and the vagina
pk: Therapeutic response over weeks of continued use
Tazarotenic acid Cmax ~8 hours after topical dose
Tazarotenic acid half-life approximately 18 hours after topical application
Once-daily application; tazarotenic acid is >99% protein bound and eliminated in urine and feces
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); excursions permitted -5 to 30 C
pearls: Topical retinoid for plaque psoriasis and acne - normalizes keratinocyte differentiation
Strictly contraindicated in pregnancy: confirm a negative pregnancy test and effective contraception in women of childbearing potential
Local irritation (burning, redness, peeling) is the main limiting effect - start low strength and apply to dry skin
Causes photosensitivity - daily sunscreen and avoidance of UV exposure are essential
Apply only to affected lesions; protecting surrounding normal skin reduces irritation
missed: If an evening application is missed, skip it and apply the next dose at the usual evening time - do not apply extra to make up for a missed dose, as this increases irritation.
overdose: Excessive topical use may lead to marked redness, peeling, or discomfort. Tazarotene is not for oral use; oral ingestion may produce effects like excessive intake of vitamin A (hypervitaminosis A) or other retinoids. If oral ingestion occurs, monitor the patient and provide appropriate supportive measures as necessary.
